newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland resumes IRA prisoner release programme.
newsitem.headline: Ireland resumes IRA prisoner release programme.

text.p: The Irish government on Monday resumed early releases of jailed IRA prisoners to reward the guerrillas for their July 20 ceasefire.
The Justice Ministry said two Irish Republican Army prisoners would be released, reviving a programme which was stopped when the IRA ended a 17-month ceasefire in February 1996.
Gerard Burke, serving a four-year sentence for robbery, and Thomas Flynn, jailed for six months for assault, were to be freed from Port Laoise maximum security prison near Dublin later on Wednesday.
Under normal circumstances they would have been freed in July and October next year.
Both are low-level members of the guerrillas, who have fought a 28-year to end British rule of Northern Ireland.
They called a second truce on July 20 to get their political wing, Sinn Fein, invited to Northern Ireland peace talks which start in September.

Sinn Fein is calling for the release of hundreds of IRA prisoners in British, Irish and Northern Irish jails as what it calls a confidence-building measure to enhance the atmosphere at the peace talks.
Britain's Northern Ireland Secretary said in remarks published at the weekend that if the IRA ceasefire held, "all options become open."

The Irish government freed about 30 prisoners in batches until the guerrillas ended their first truce by bombing London's Canary Wharf business complex at the start of a new campaign in February 1996.
It was not immediately clear how many IRA prisoners remain in Irish jails but the number was thought to be less than 20.
